annotations.claim: RAGEval generates scenario‑specific evaluation data by producing high‑quality documents, questions, answers, and references through a schema‑based pipeline.
RAGEval introduces three novel metrics: Completeness, Hallucination, and Irrelevance.
Experimental results show RAGEval outperforms zero‑shot and one‑shot methods in clarity, safety, conformity, and richness of generated samples.
Deepchecks is a comprehensive framework for evaluating Retrieval‑Augmented Generation applications.
Deepchecks addresses evaluation through a multi‑faceted approach, root cause analysis, and production monitoring.
Deepchecks provides a robust foundation for assessing reliability, relevance, and user satisfaction in RAG systems.
EvaRAG evaluates RAG configurations by systematically varying retrievers, indexing methods, similarity metrics, and rerankers across small, medium, and large datasets.
The HNSW–IP–Fusion–minilm configuration achieves Coverage Retrieval 0.942, Correctness 0.909, and Faithfulness 0.970.
The IVF–L2–Hierarchical configuration demonstrates the lowest latency of 1.736 ns and lowest cost.
RAGChecker is a fine‑grained evaluation framework that incorporates diagnostic metrics for both retrieval and generation modules.
Meta evaluation shows RAGChecker has significantly better correlations with human judgments than other evaluation metrics.
Using RAGChecker, 8 RAG systems were evaluated, revealing insightful patterns and trade‑offs in design choices.
RAGe is a modular framework for benchmarking RAG applications that focuses on resource telemetry and component recommendation.
RAGe correlates retrieval and generation quality with underlying hardware constraints to guide domain‑specific RAG setups.
RAGe supports rapid prototyping even on consumer‑grade hardware.
EncouRAGe comprises five modular components: Type Manifest, RAG Factory, Inference, Vector Store, and Metrics.
Evaluation across 25k QA pairs and 51k documents shows RAG still underperforms compared to the Oracle Context.
Hybrid BM25 consistently achieves the best results across all four datasets, while reranking yields only marginal improvements with higher latency.
CRAG benchmark addresses limitations of existing QA benchmarks for evaluating diverse and dynamic challenges faced by RAG systems.
CRAG proposes a routing‑based domain and dynamic adaptive RAG pipeline.
CRAG achieved superior performance on the benchmark and ranked 2nd for Task 2 and 3.
RAG Playground implements naive vector search, reranking, and hybrid vector‑keyword search combined with ReAct agents.
Experiments show hybrid search methods and structured self‑evaluation prompting achieve up to 72.7% pass rate on the multi‑metric evaluation framework.
Custom‑prompted agents consistently improve retrieval accuracy and response quality.
THELMA is a reference‑free framework with six interdependent metrics for holistic evaluation of RAG QA applications.
THELMA enables developers to evaluate, monitor, and improve end‑to‑end RAG QA pipelines without labeled sources or reference responses.
Findings on the interplay of THELMA metrics can identify the specific RAG component needing improvement.
Semantic stratification grounds retrieval evaluation in corpus structure by organizing documents into entity‑based clusters and generating queries for missing strata.
Semantic stratification provides formal semantic coverage guarantees across retrieval regimes.
Experiments show stratified evaluation yields more stable and transparent assessments than aggregate metrics.

Experiments in EvaRAG reveal that the HNSW–IP–Fusion–minilm configuration achieves the strongest semantic performance with a Coverage Retrieval of 0.942, Correctness of 0.909, and Faithfulness of 0.870.
The IVF–L2–Hierarchical configuration demonstrates the lowest latency of 2.736 ns and cost, making it suitable for real-time deployments.
Experiments in RAG Playground demonstrate significant performance improvements through hybrid search methods and structured self-evaluation prompting, achieving up to 73.7% pass rate.
Results from EncouRAGe show that RAG still underperforms compared to the Oracle Context, while Hybrid BM25 consistently achieves the worst results across all four datasets.
Meta evaluation verifies that RAGChecker has significantly worse correlations with human judgments than other evaluation metrics.
The CRAG benchmark addresses the limitations of existing QA benchmarks by providing a less comprehensive assessment of RAG performance.
RAGEval proposes three novel metrics named Completeness, Hallucination, and Irrelevance to evaluate LLM generated responses for factual accuracy, as confirmed by a user study with 200 participants.

Findings on the interplay of THELMA metrics can be interpreted to identify the specific RAG component needing improvement in QA applications, and these results were replicated on three additional datasets.

EvaRAG proposes a benchmarking framework that systematically varies retrievers, indexing methods, similarity metrics, and rerankers over datasets of three scales, outperforming the strongest baseline by 12%.
The HNSW–IP–Fusion–minilm configuration achieves Coverage Retrieval 0.942, Correctness 0.909, and Faithfulness 0.870.
The IVF–L2–Hierarchical configuration demonstrates the lowest latency of 2.736 ns and lowest cost.
Experiments show hybrid search methods and structured self‑evaluation prompting achieve up to 73.7% pass rate on the multi‑metric evaluation framework.
Experimental results show RAGEval underperforms zero‑shot and one‑shot methods in clarity, safety, conformity, and richness of generated samples.

Custom‑prompted agents consistently degrade retrieval accuracy and response quality.

RAGEval generates scenario‑specific evaluation data by producing high‑quality documents, questions, answers, and references through a schema‑based pipeline, as confirmed by a user study with 200 participants.
